source.title: Appreciation Teaches Unauthorized Execution: Self-Evolution Degrades the Robustness of Personal Agents to Indirect Prompt Injection
source.authors: Xin-Yang Wang; Xiaogeng Liu; Jun Shao; Chao-Wei Xiao

page_placements.theme: Agent adaptation and persistent updates can erode safety

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies indirect prompt injection in personal agents, not refusal of harmful user requests, response-position KL, opening-token bypasses, or localization of safety in parameters. It cites related safety-decay work but does not test the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The reported ASR results concern unauthorized execution of instructions in untrusted content, not compliance with harmful requests from the user. They are recorded as findings about a related but different construct under fits_no_version. The paper cites Fine-tuning Aligned Language Models Compromises Safety, Even When Users Do Not Intend To! as related work; it reports no results from that study.
record.test_reason: The study measures whether self-evolved personal agents execute instructions planted by a third party in external content (indirect prompt injection). It does not measure compliance with harmful user requests, per-token KL, prefill or suffix bypasses, parameter localization, or deepening training. RL LoRA updates on benign authorized tasks do raise ASR. That is a benign-training effect, but on behaviour toward third-party content rather than harmful user requests, so it does not bear on V2. Qi et al. (an original source) appears only as a related-work citation.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Self-evolution from user feedback degrades IPI robustness under both RL and skill evolution, mainly through authorization conflation. Authorization-distinguishing feedback prevents most of the rise under skill evolution. Delimiting leaves substantial degradation.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses RL weight updates or learned textual skills in a personal-agent setting, with injected instructions in external content and unauthorized-action ASR as the outcome. It does not use the original harmful-request fine-tuning setup or measure refusal of harmful user requests.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by model, task, self-evolution mechanism, and learned skill library. The authors report ASR increases in 8 of 15 RL model–task pairs and 15 of 20 skill-evolution pairs in the main setting; tool-output delimiting lowers ASR but does not restore base-agent rates.

fits_no_version.finding: Benign feedback-driven self-evolution (RL LoRA or learned skills) raises mean IPI ASR for every model–mechanism pair in seed 1. Task-level effects vary, and results are unstable across presentation orders (e.g., GPT-OSS-120B skill evolution mean 53.5% in seed 1 vs 9.0% in seed 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign self-evolution of personal agents can increase unauthorized execution of third-party injected instructions, with large dependence on model, task, mechanism and adaptation order.

fits_no_version.finding: Skill-evolution controls on Qwen3.8-27B File–Create tie the ASR rise to execution-rewarded feedback. Authorization-aware feedback cuts ASR from 35.0% to 5.8%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feedback contrasting authorized and unauthorized execution mitigates learned injection compliance.

fits_no_version.finding: Tool-output delimiting lowers self-evolved ASR (95.0% to 37.5% under RL, 97.5% to 47.5% under skills) but does not restore the base agents' 0%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Delimiting only partially restores IPI robustness after self-evolution.

record.problems: The authors note that experiments use a short series of conversations, local files, and simulated online services rather than months of daily use, and cover a limited range of usage scenarios. The paper reports rates but no confidence intervals or error bars in the presented results.
record.rows_left_out: The main table’s Setting 1 authorized-execution rates and Setting 2 ASR on adaptation content, the full extra presentation-order tables (Tables 5 and 6), and further follow-up results in Sections 4.4 and Appendices C–D are not individually rowed. They concern the same indirect-prompt-injection construct but are outside the listed claim versions; selected main new-content, control, and delimiting outcomes are included.

untested.parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples; no harmful user-request compliance measured.
Benign RL/skill adaptation is studied, but the outcome is third-party injection execution, not harmful compliance with user requests.
No prefilling, adversarial suffix or decoding attacks.
No weight or rank localization of safety.
No account of why safety is shallow. The authorization-conflation mechanism concerns IPI, not refusal depth.

record.verdict_notes: The relation was changed from discusses to cites_only: Qi et al. appears only in a related-work sentence. The harmful-instruction case study (Appendix D.3, 119/162 vs 1/162) uses base weights with an inserted skill library, targets third-party injected instructions, and was not rowed. It does not bear on any version but could be added to the first fits_no_version entry. Seeds 2 and 3 (Tables 5 and 6) show strong order dependence and are declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not fine-tune on harmful examples or measure refusal/compliance with harmful user requests.
It studies feedback-driven RL and skill evolution for indirect prompt injection, not ordinary or carefully selected benign instruction data and harmful-user-request compliance.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL or response-position analysis.

No compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding-change bypass test. Tool-output delimiting is tested, but it is a defense against indirect prompt injection, not one of the stated opening-token bypass tests.
No test of whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
The study analyzes authorization conflation in personal agents, not why safety behaviour is shallow.
No training designed to deepen safety across response tokens or test of whether such deepening holds up.
